title: Indian National Saka Calendar
intro: India's national civil calendar is a modern date system that uses the Saka Era and twelve named months alongside the Gregorian calendar.
summary: A solar calendar with twelve months. Chaitra begins on 22 March in ordinary Gregorian years and 21 March in leap years.
origin: India adopted the Indian National Calendar in 1957. Its year count uses the Saka Era; the calendar was designed for consistent official use across regions.
structure: The calendar begins with Chaitra. Its month lengths follow the Gregorian solar year, with the first month adjusted in leap years.
diagram_caption: 12 SOLAR MONTHS / A SAKA ERA YEAR
pattern_note: Chaitra length changes with Gregorian leap years. The names refer to the national civil calendar, not every regional Indian religious calendar.
history: The Saka national calendar is used for certain official Indian purposes. Many other regional lunisolar and solar traditions continue to be used for religious and cultural events.
example: Gregorian 22 March 2026 falls at the start of Chaitra in Saka year 1948 under the normal-year convention.
limits: This model represents India's modern national calendar, not the entire range of historic Indian date systems. Calendar conventions must be distinguished from regional practice.
